FROMGIT: PM / OPP: Introduce a power estimation helper The Energy Model (EM) framework provides an API to let drivers register the active power of CPUs. The drivers are expected to provide a callback method which estimates the power consumed by a CPU at each available performance levels. How exactly this should be implemented, however, depends on the platform. On some systems, PM_OPP knows the voltage and frequency at which CPUs can run. When coupled with the CPU 'capacitance' (as provided by the 'dynamic-power-coefficient' devicetree binding), it is possible to estimate the dynamic power consumption of a CPU as P = C * V^2 * f, with C its capacitance and V and f respectively the voltage and frequency of the OPP. The Intelligent Power Allocator (IPA) thermal governor already implements that estimation method, in the thermal framework. However, this power estimation method can be applied to any platform where all the parameters are known (C, V and f), and not only those suffering thermal issues. As such, the code implementing this feature can be re-used to also populate the EM framework now used by EAS. As a first step, introduce in PM_OPP a helper function which CPUFreq drivers can use to register into the EM framework. This duplicates the power estimation done in IPA until it can be migrated to using the EM framework. This will be done later, once the EM framework has support for at least all platforms currently supported by IPA. Signed-off-by: Quentin Perret <quentin.perret@arm.com> Tested-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Signed-off-by: Viresh Kumar <viresh.kumar@linaro.org> (cherry picked from commit a4f342b9607d8c2034d3135cbbb11b4028be3678 git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/vireshk/pm.git opp/linux-next) BUG=b:111527336, b:116109744 TEST=build for cheza Change-Id: I841b5e50ef057ca37d7ee8f20a0515209d909b3e Signed-off-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1455078 Reviewed-by: Evan Green <evgreen@chromium.org>

bluetooth: add suspend/resume infrastructure per powerd guidelines This CL extends the suspend_manager.cc in btdispatch to support a generic interface of BlueZ and NewBlue with the powerd, required for the system operations of suspend and resume. The dispatcher relays powerd notifications to BlueZ and to NewBlue, for them to perform any task needed prior suspend or after resume, and acknowledge back to powerd when both are done. New D-Bus messages were defined for the interaction between the dispatcher and BlueZ. No support is added for NewBlue in this change, however the generic infra in the btdispatcher can be extended to NewBlue in the future (b:123933149) Refer to b:123932305 for url of powerd guidelines. BUG=b:123932305 TEST=suspend and resume of system when discovery is running/not running Follow powerd logs to verify correct states. repeatable attempts to verify stability. Verify suspend and resume of discovery when UI tries to connect still working as before. FROMLIST: ath10k: Enable Factory Test Mode for WCN3990 The support to put WCN3990 firmware into Factory test mode is not present currently. The WCN3990 firmware can operate in Factory test mode based on the mode it receives in the wlan enable message from the host driver. When the host driver is started in testmode send the operating mode as UTF mode, to the WCN3990 firmware, in the wlan enable message to start the firmware in Factory test mode. cups: Fix for PPD generation in lpadmin (URF format as default) The problem occurs for IPP Everywhere printers supporting both URF and PWG formats. During generation of PPD file, previous CUPS version (from R71) choose PWG format as default if printer does not support PDF. The current CUPS version (shipped with R72) prefers URF format over PWG. This patch changes this behaviour and makes CUPS to prefer PWG format over URF.
